content.comment_body: My [product_name] Operator Device shows the message 'BM No Resp Press ESC'. I have tried rebooting and other suggested options, but nothing resets the device. I even reprogrammed the controller, but the issue remains. Any advice would be appreciated.

If your Operator Device displays 'BM No response', please verify all LAN cables, IP addresses, and subnet masks on both ends. It’s possible that the IP address of the controller was altered in the device settings and is no longer accessible. Regards, [user_name]

This controller is an older [company_name] model [article_no]. When running the diagnostic you suggested, it says 'the connected base module does not support network communication.' This setup worked for months and only recently showed this error after turning it on.

Are you sure your device is actually a [article_no]? If so, this version does not support Ethernet and lacks an internet connection or RJ45 port. Also, is your Operator Device a TD or TD E? The TDE is not compatible with a [article_no] version.
To connect this setup to a computer, I use the specific [company_name] cable. This unit is older and does not have an Ethernet port.
I understand. Could you clarify: is your Operator Device a TD or a TD E? Please provide the article number, such as [article_no].
For context, I am not an expert with these [company_name] modules.
I have attached a picture showing a [version_no] controller connected to an Operator Device using a specialized serial cable. This is the Operator Device cable, article number [article_no].
The Operator Device part number is [article_no].

That number refers to the controller module, not the Operator Device. The older Operator Device uses article number [article_no] and communicates with older controllers using a serial cable. A newer Operator Device version for the [version_no] uses article number [article_no], which connects to the latest controller via Ethernet TCP/IP.
Sorry for the confusion. The Operator Device I am using is article number [article_no].
Got it, you have the older Operator Device ([article_no]) that connects to the [version_no] controller using a TD cable (part number [article_no]), as previously mentioned.

Yes, that is the cable used to connect the controller to the display. I have a USB cable to download the program to the controller. Reinstalling the software appears to work, but the same error still appears during operation.
Please check if the TD cable is firmly plugged into the left side of the controller and that it has a solid connection. Otherwise, my only suggestion is to start a support request.
The cable appears to be properly inserted and well connected. It doesn't seem loose.
[user_name], I tried another cable and now everything works again. I'm unsure why, since the original cable hadn’t been moved for months, but the system is operating properly now.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced a persistent 'BM No Resp Press ESC' message on an Operator Device connected to an older base module lacking Ethernet support. The discussion highlighted confusion surrounding device compatibility, correct cable choice, and network communication capabilities in legacy hardware. Despite various troubleshooting attempts like resets and reprogramming, clear guidance for resolving issues with older modules and verifying hardware compatibility was missing until a faulty cable was replaced.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for straightforward troubleshooting guidance, clear compatibility details, and reliable solutions for issues with older [company_name] hardware setups, particularly those without Ethernet functionality.
